success_patterns: Trajectory 2: the clue referred to an image the agent cannot see ('the molecule whose structure is seen here'). The agent ignored the missing picture and answered from the textual hooks that remained (the function 'used as a bleach' plus 'molecule'), picking the entity that recurs in passage titles and text (Hydrogen peroxide). It kept the full standard name and used no extra qualifiers.

Trajectory 1: the agent matched the clue verbatim against an all-caps flashcard line ('...INTO THIS LANGUAGE, WELSH.') and copied the final item. Many other passages (Welsh Bible, Welsh New Testament) corroborated it. Rule 3 already covers this, so no edit is needed.
Both answers were short, bare and in the form a trivia key would use ('Welsh', 'hydrogen peroxide'). They did not echo the clue's nouns ('language', 'substance'), which is already covered by Rule 4.

patch.reasoning: Rule 3 and Rule 4 already explain the Welsh success. The skill has no guidance for clues that point to a picture, audio or video the agent cannot perceive ('seen here', 'shown here', 'heard here'). Trajectory 2 shows the right approach: treat the media cue as decoration and resolve the clue from its remaining textual descriptors (function or use, class) together with the entity the passages repeat. A short note encodes this without touching other rules.

edits.target: - Jokes, asides and filler in the clue ('(If I eat it, can I hear the ocean?)', 'Need help in this subject? Call up...') are decoration.
edits.content: - Media cues ('seen here', 'shown here', 'heard here', 'pictured', 'whose structure is seen here') point to an image, video or audio clue you cannot perceive. Do not answer 'cannot tell' and do not guess from the missing picture. Drop the cue and resolve the clue from the textual hooks that remain: the function or use ('used as a bleach'), the class ('molecule', 'substance') and any named anchor. Choose the single entity that those hooks and the passage titles and snippets repeatedly tie together ('Hydrogen peroxide' for a 'simple molecule used as a bleach'). Give its standard full name without the category words the clue supplies. If passages are noisy, use your own knowledge to pick the well-known entity that fits every remaining hook.
